question.problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\text{_____},\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16.$ What is the second component of $f?$

current_example.problem:
$$
\mathbf{f}(\theta,\phi) = \big\langle 5 \cos\theta\sin\phi, \: \text{_____}, \: 5 \cos\phi \big\rangle
$$

The vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(\theta,\phi)$ above parametrizes the sphere defined in Cartesian coordinates as $x^2+y^2+z^2=25.$ What is the second component of $\mathbf{f}?$
current_example.worked_solution:
The given equation generates a sphere of radius $5$ centered at the origin.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =5.$

If $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found using the following formulas:

$$
x = \rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \qquad
y = \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \qquad 
z = \rho\cos\phi.
$$

 

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨5\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi)$ and $\phi \in [-\pi,\pi].$

Therefore, the second component of $\mathbf{f}$ is ${\color{black} 5 \sin\theta\sin\phi}.$
